samples.summary: CLI consent page test never asserts that the continue link carries `nonce` and `code_challenge`
samples.evidence: `renders the interstitial instead of starting the login` only asserts the HTML contains `http://127.0.0.1:9876`, `cli_confirm=tok-123` and `/auth/github?mode=cli&port=9876`. `renderCliConsent` also puts `nonce` and `code_challenge` on the href, and the guard hard-refuses a resumed start missing either (`BadRequestException('Missing or invalid nonce' / 'code_challenge')`, github-auth.guard.ts). If either parameter were dropped from the link, every CLI login would 400 after the consent click and the entire suite would stay green — no other test drives the render→click round trip (grep for `nonce` in auth.controller.spec.ts only hits the callback tests; github-auth.guard.spec.ts builds its confirmed query by hand rather than from the rendered page).
searchedFor: read github-auth.guard.spec.ts (confirmedContext/cliQuery build the query literally)

samples.summary: New `escapeHtml` helper has no test with hostile input
samples.evidence: `escapeHtml` is introduced to sanitize values interpolated into the consent page. The only assertion that touches it is `expect(html).toContain('/auth/github?mode=cli&port=9876')`, which exercises `&` only. The `nonce` reaching the page is length-bounded (≤128) but not charset-restricted by `boundedToken` (only `code_challenge` gets `/^[A-Za-z0-9\-._~]+$/`), so `"`, `<` and `'` can arrive; no test feeds such a nonce through `githubAuth` to prove the escaping holds.
searchedFor: read the 'CLI consent page' describe in auth.controller.spec.ts

samples.summary: New login-page `?error=` banner ships with no frontend test
samples.evidence: `LoginForm` now reads `useSearchParams()` and renders an alert with `ERROR_MESSAGES[error] ?? FALLBACK_ERROR` — a new user-facing behavior that is the visible half of the backend's `/login?error=login_state` redirect. No test file covers it: the only component test under src/components is `__tests__/datasource-dialog.test.tsx`, and grepping the frontend for `login_state` finds only the component, the page and the README. The frontend also has no `tsc` lane, so nothing else exercises this file.

samples.summary: The new `command` plumbing through the import/upload/download orchestrators is untested end to end
samples.evidence: `runDocsImport`, `runNotesImport`, `runSlidesImport`, `runFilesUpload` and `runFilesDownload` all gained a `command` arg that the actions fill with `commandPath(this)`, but no test asserts the field arrives in their envelopes: grepping `command` across packages/cli/test matches only output.test.ts, ctx.test.ts, login-callback.test.ts, docs-content.test.ts, schema.test.ts, tabs/version/namespaces/bin. docs-import.test.ts has no match for `command`/`HTTP_ERROR`, and files-download.test.ts never parses the stderr envelope. A dropped `command: commandPath(this)` at any of those call sites would go unnoticed; only `errorEnvelope` itself is unit-tested.

samples.summary: The CLI consent gate is never exercised under the `__Host-` (secure) cookie naming
samples.evidence: `hasConfirmation` reads `loginCookieName(configService, CLI_CONFIRM_COOKIE)` while the interstitial sets the same prefixed name. Every consent-gate test in github-auth.guard.spec.ts (`confirmedContext`, lines 103-108, and the `CLI consent gate` describe) uses the plain-http `configService`, so the prefixed path is only covered for `OAUTH_STATE_COOKIE`. A name mismatch on secure deployments would loop the consent page forever with the suite green.

samples.summary: `announceLoginUrl`'s TTY branch and its write-failure fallback are untested
samples.evidence: login-callback.test.ts only runs under a non-TTY stderr, so it covers the file-writing branch (`expect(notices.some((n) => n.includes(urlPath))).toBe(true)`). Neither the `process.stderr.isTTY` branch (which prints the URL, including the nonce, to stderr) nor the `catch` fallback (`Could not open a browser…`) is covered — a regression that printed the secret-bearing URL in the non-TTY case, or wrote it world-readable, would only be caught by the one existing path.

login-callback.test.ts covers a 401 (`UNAUTHORIZED`, exit 2) and a 502 (`SYSTEM`, exit 2). `codeForStatus` also has a third branch returning `HTTP_ERROR` with `process.exit(1)`; no test drives a 4xx other than 401/403, so that mapping is unverified.

The guard throws `InternalServerErrorException('Cannot start a login session')` when the response cannot set cookies; grepping the backend for `Cannot start a login session` finds only the source line, and github-auth.guard.spec.ts always supplies a response with `cookie`/`clearCookie`.
searchedFor: grep 'InternalServerError|Cannot start a login session' packages/backend

samples.summary: The pino serializer wiring of `logSafeUrl` is not covered
samples.evidence: log-safe-url.spec.ts thoroughly tests the pure function, but nothing asserts that the `req` serializer in app.module.ts actually calls it — a revert of that one line would leave every log-safe-url test green while auth query strings return to the access log.

finding.summary: CLI consent page test never asserts that the continue link carries `nonce` and `code_challenge`
finding.evidence: `renders the interstitial instead of starting the login` only asserts the HTML contains `http://127.0.0.1:9876`, `cli_confirm=tok-123` and `/auth/github?mode=cli&port=9876`. `renderCliConsent` also puts `nonce` and `code_challenge` on the href, and the guard hard-refuses a resumed start missing either (`BadRequestException('Missing or invalid nonce' / 'code_challenge')`, github-auth.guard.ts). If either parameter were dropped from the link, every CLI login would 400 after the consent click and the entire suite would stay green — no other test drives the render→click round trip (grep for `nonce` in auth.controller.spec.ts only hits the callback tests; github-auth.guard.spec.ts builds its confirmed query by hand rather than from the rendered page).
searchedFor: read github-auth.guard.spec.ts (confirmedContext/cliQuery build the query literally)

verdict.reason: Verified independently. renderCliConsent (auth.controller.ts:145-153) puts nonce and code_challenge on the continue href, but the sole test that invokes the render (auth.controller.spec.ts:539-561) asserts only 'http://127.0.0.1:9876', 'cli_confirm=tok-123' and '/auth/github?mode=cli&port=9876'. Since URLSearchParams preserves insertion order (mode, port, nonce, code_challenge, cli_confirm), removing nonce and/or code_challenge leaves all three assertions passing — the test cannot fail on that regression, even though the fixture supplies both values (lines 546-547). I searched wide for a counterexample and found none: `githubAuth(`/`__cliConsent` appear only in that one spec; github-auth.guard.spec.ts:103-129 builds cliQuery/confirmedContext literally rather than parsing the rendered page; auth.controller.spec.ts:205-236 mints CLI state directly via cliAuthStore.createState, bypassing the consent page; no backend e2e spec touches /auth/github with mode=cli (only an env default at test/helpers/integration-helpers.ts:94); packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts:285-290 asserts the CLI-generated start URL, not the server-rendered link; and a repo-wide grep for 'Continue sign-in'/'class="continue"' hits only auth.controller.ts:185. So a behavior essential to the CLI login round trip (the link carrying the two parameters the guard hard-refuses when absent) has no meaningful test — a missing-test gap in the test-adequacy lane.
